public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of May 2025, there is no concretely implemented international AI governance and no US national AI agency, and the US is no longer even well positioned to detect and address AI-escalated cybercrime.

statement.excerpt: We have no concretely implemented international AI governance, no national AI agency; we are no longer even positioned well to detect and address AI-escalated cybercrime.
statement.document_title: Two Years Ago Today in AI History: The Tale of An About-face in AI Regulation

from_speaker: no concretely implemented international AI governance
our_interpretation: This is a three-part observation about the position at publication on May 16, 2025.
For these institutional and operational claims, the target is the publication-day state rather than a financial reporting period.
International governance ordinarily includes operating cross-border oversight arrangements, although the hearing context could imply a binding international regulator.
National AI agency means a dedicated US AI regulator in this context; an AI research office is not automatically equivalent.
The cybercrime clause requires evidence of inadequate detection and response capacity and deterioration from an earlier position. Proposed cuts alone do not establish either.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish the absence of implemented international governance and a dedicated US AI regulator, together with an assessed deterioration leaving US AI-cybercrime defenses inadequate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records establish qualifying governance or a dedicated regulator, or demonstrate adequate and undiminished AI-cybercrime detection and response capacity. A split across established components warrants mixed.

evidence.explanation: Actual submissions establish more than an unfulfilled pledge before the post. The framework was voluntary, and this earlier observation does not establish a binding international regulator or its precise publication-day status.
Reporting from an internal agency meeting documents planned reductions and uncertainty about approval. It does not measure completed reductions or the adequacy of AI-cybercrime defenses on May 16.
